questions.question_text: The heights of a large group of adults are normally distributed with a mean of $170$ cm and a standard deviation of $8$ cm. Find the probability that a randomly chosen adult has a height between $162$ cm and $178$ cm.

options.why: Halved the band, giving only the part between $170$ cm and $178$ cm.
Added $0.5$ to $0.34$, which gives the probability of a height below $178$ cm instead.
Gave the two tails outside the band rather than the band itself.

questions.question_text: The masses of chickens on a farm are normally distributed with a mean of $1.8$ kg and a standard deviation of $0.15$ kg. Find the probability that a randomly chosen chicken has a mass greater than $1.95$ kg.

options.why: Left the whole leftover $1 - 0.68 = 0.32$ in one tail instead of halving it between the two tails.
Gave the probability that a chicken is lighter than $1.95$ kg.
Gave the area from the mean up to $1.95$ kg rather than the area beyond it.

questions.question_text: The times taken by a bus to complete a route are normally distributed with a mean of $46$ minutes and a standard deviation of $3$ minutes. Find the probability that a randomly chosen trip takes less than $55$ minutes.

options.why: Gave the band within three standard deviations, leaving out the trips shorter than $37$ minutes.
Gave only the area from the mean up to $55$ minutes, omitting the $0.5$ below the mean.
Gave the probability that a trip takes more than $55$ minutes.

questions.question_text: The lengths of nails are normally distributed with a mean of $50$ mm and a standard deviation of $1$ mm. Find the probability that a randomly chosen nail has a length either between $48$ mm and $49$ mm or between $51$ mm and $52$ mm.

options.why: Gave the whole region from $48$ mm to $52$ mm instead of only the two outer bands.
Used the two bands between $2\sigma$ and $3\sigma$ instead of the bands between $\sigma$ and $2\sigma$.
Gave the whole region from the mean out to $2\sigma$ instead of only the two bands between $\sigma$ and $2\sigma$.

questions.question_text: The marks in an examination are normally distributed with a mean of $55$ and a standard deviation of $10$. Find the probability that a randomly chosen mark lies between $25$ and $65$.

options.why: Used $0.5$ for the region below the mean instead of the $0.4985$ that reaches only down to $25$.
Used the $0.16$ tail above $65$ instead of the $0.34$ between $55$ and $65$.
Added the $0.0015$ tail below $25$ to $0.34$ instead of the $0.4985$ between $25$ and $55$.

questions.question_text: A crop of $900$ tomato plants has yields that are normally distributed with a mean of $40$ tomatoes and a standard deviation of $6$ tomatoes. How many plants are expected to yield more than $46$ tomatoes?

options.why: Used $0.34$, the area from the mean up to $46$, instead of the $0.16$ beyond it.
Used $0.84$, which is the probability of yielding fewer than $46$ tomatoes.
Used the whole $0.68$ band within one standard deviation instead of the upper tail.

questions.question_text: In a town, the weekly water use of $2400$ households is normally distributed with a mean of $1500$ L and a standard deviation of $200$ L. How many households are expected to use between $1100$ L and $1500$ L?

options.why: Used $0.95$, the whole band from $1100$ L to $1900$ L, instead of the half below the mean.
Used $0.68$, the band within one standard deviation, instead of the $0.475$ region.
Used $0.5$, counting every household below the mean rather than only those above $1100$ L.

questions.question_text: The times taken by workers to assemble a part are normally distributed with a mean of $72$ seconds and a standard deviation of $6$ seconds. One worker takes $90$ seconds. Which statement best describes this time?

options.text: It is $3$ standard deviations above the mean, and only about $0.15\%$ of times are this long, so it is unusual.
It is $3$ standard deviations above the mean, and about $0.3\%$ of times are this long, so it is unusual.
options.why: Left the whole leftover $100\% - 99.7\% = 0.3\%$ in the upper tail instead of halving it between the two tails.

options.text: It is $3$ standard deviations above the mean, and about $49.85\%$ of times are this long, so it is not unusual.
options.why: Used the region from the mean up to $90$ seconds instead of the region beyond $90$ seconds.

options.text: It is $2$ standard deviations above the mean, and about $2.5\%$ of times are this long, so it is unusual.
options.why: Counted $90 - 72 = 18$ seconds as $2$ standard deviations instead of $3$.
